findings.reason: The protected SQL solution groups Orders by (customer_id, product_id) to count orders, applies DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_count DESC) in a CTE, filters for frequency_rank = 1, and inner joins Products to retrieve product_name. Using DENSE_RANK guarantees that all products tied for a customer's maximum frequency are retained. The solution is canonical, optimal, and concise; no candidate is required.

Grouping Orders by customer and product counts occurrences per pair. DENSE_RANK assigns rank 1 to all products matching the maximum count for that customer. Filtering frequency_rank = 1 retains all maximum-frequency products including ties, while customers with no orders are naturally omitted.

Grouping r order rows into g distinct customer-product pairs and ranking takes O(r log r) time, and joining Products takes O(g + p) time. Working space is O(g). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs columns customer_id, product_id, and product_name, handles tied maximum product frequencies per customer, and excludes customers with zero orders.

The approach accurately details grouping orders per customer and product, applying DENSE_RANK for ties, joining Products post-ranking, and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover correlated subqueries, ROW_NUMBER tie-loss bugs, per-customer MAX subquery CTEs, single products, ties, and orderless customers.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both use the same CTE order counting, DENSE_RANK window function, Products join, and rank-1 filter with SHA-256 digests ca3fb01885178cbac2b461c07a9f06907c406c536e88faac92db45968f16acb4 and e2682530de9e880444ae9c7572015706930fb2f430e0bad869f27cc769ad4c68. Verified submission remains untouched.

Statement structure and factual evidence confirmed Customers, Orders, and Products schemas, three examples, two constraints, and 7 tables in reference mode. Bound to content SHA-256 f664f3fcf4447d4c2472c9e017471858bb4799b05c7420a91fd1e917f71df270.
